name: SPIRIT 2013
source: Chan A-W, Tetzlaff JM, Altman DG, Laupacis A, Gotzsche PC, Krleza-Jeric K, et al. SPIRIT 2013 Statement: Defining Standard Protocol Items for Clinical Trials. Ann Intern Med. 2013;158(3):200-207. https://www.spirit-statement.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/01/SPIRIT-Checklist-download-8Jan13.pdf | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5114123/

items.text: Provide a descriptive title stating study design, population, interventions, and trial acronym if used.
State the trial registration identifier and registry name, or intended registry if unregistered.
Include all items from the World Health Organization Trial Registration Data Set.
State the protocol date and version identifier.
Describe sources and types of financial, material, and other trial support.
List names, affiliations, and roles of protocol contributors.
Provide the name and contact details of the trial sponsor.
Describe sponsor and funder roles and authority across trial design, conduct, analysis, and publication.
Describe composition and responsibilities of oversight groups such as steering or adjudication committees.
Explain the research question and rationale, summarizing prior evidence of intervention benefits and harms.
Justify the choice of comparator interventions.
State the specific trial objectives or hypotheses.
Describe the trial type, allocation ratio, and framework such as superiority or noninferiority.
Describe study settings, countries of data collection, and where to obtain the site list.
Specify participant inclusion and exclusion criteria, plus center or provider eligibility if applicable.
Describe each group's intervention, including administration details, sufficiently to permit replication.
Specify criteria for modifying or discontinuing allocated interventions for an individual participant.
Describe strategies to promote and monitor participant adherence to intervention protocols.
Specify relevant concomitant care and interventions permitted or prohibited during the trial.
Define primary, secondary, and other outcomes, including measurement variable, metric, aggregation, and time points.
Present the schedule of enrollment, interventions, assessments, and visits, ideally as a schematic figure.
Report the target sample size and the clinical and statistical assumptions used to calculate it.
Describe strategies planned to achieve adequate participant enrollment.

sections.title: Methods: Assignment of interventions (for controlled trials)

items.text: Describe random allocation sequence generation and stratification factors, keeping restriction details separately concealed.
Describe the mechanism used to implement and conceal the allocation sequence until assignment.
Specify who generates the allocation sequence, enrolls participants, and assigns interventions.
State who will be blinded after assignment and how blinding will be achieved.
State circumstances allowing unblinding and the procedure for revealing allocated interventions.

sections.title: Methods: Data collection, management, and analysis

items.text: Describe plans and instruments for collecting outcome and baseline data, plus quality assurance processes.
Describe plans to promote retention and collect outcomes from participants who discontinue or deviate.
Describe data entry, coding, security, storage, and quality-check procedures.
Describe planned statistical methods for analyzing primary and secondary outcomes.
Describe planned methods for additional analyses such as subgroup and adjusted analyses.
Define analysis populations for non-adherence and statistical methods for handling missing data.
Describe the data monitoring committee's composition, independence, role, and charter, or why none is needed.
Describe planned interim analyses, stopping guidelines, and who holds final trial termination authority.
Describe plans for collecting, assessing, reporting, and managing adverse events and unintended effects.
Describe trial conduct auditing frequency and procedures, including independence from investigators and sponsor.
Describe plans for obtaining institutional review board or research ethics committee approval.
Describe plans for communicating major protocol changes to ethics boards, investigators, participants, and registries.
State who will obtain informed consent or assent from participants or surrogates and how.
Describe additional consent provisions for ancillary studies using participant data or biospecimens.
Explain how personal participant data will be collected, shared, and protected throughout the trial.
Disclose financial and other competing interests for principal investigators across the trial and sites.
State who will access the final dataset and disclose any contractual restrictions on investigators.
Describe provisions for ancillary care, post-trial care, and compensation for trial-related harm.
Describe plans to communicate trial results to participants, clinicians, and the public, noting restrictions.
State authorship eligibility criteria and any planned use of professional medical writers.
Describe any plans to grant public access to the protocol, participant-level data, and code.
Attach model consent forms and related participant information materials.
Describe plans for collecting, evaluating, and storing biological specimens for current or future analyses.
